title: Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain
abstract: The proposal is to probe Majorana modes in the system when its parameters are tuned to bring it into a disentangled ground state, which occur on the parametric curves known as disorder lines (DL). In such state certain correlation functions do not depend on separation. The exact results are presented for the XY spin chain in transverse field, also called the Kitaev chain in the Majorana representation. The single Majorana modes are shown to be localized near the ends of the chain, as in the states off the DL, while the disentangled $n$-particle Majorana modes ($n \geq 2$) penetrate into the bulk without attenuation. The predicted bulk-edge effects can be detected in the specially engineered optical chains and lattices.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes Majorana fermions in a spin chain model, specifically focusing on the behavior when the system parameters place it on a 'disorder line' (DL). The key finding is that while single Majorana modes remain localized at the edges, multi-particle ($n \ge 2$) modes can penetrate deep into the bulk without decaying. This suggests a mechanism for realizing robust topological properties in engineered quantum materials.
main_problem: The research aims to investigate Majorana modes within a quantum chain when its parameters are tuned to a specific 'disentangled ground state' occurring on disorder lines (DL).
main_result: On the DL, $n$-particle Majorana modes ($n \ge 2$) penetrate into the bulk without attenuation, unlike single modes which remain localized at the ends.
method: The analysis employs the Jordan-Wigner transformation to map the spin Hamiltonian onto a system of Majorana fermions, followed by calculations of various correlation functions in the Majorana representation.
model_or_system: The physical model is the XY spin chain in transverse field, equivalent to the Kitaev chain when analyzed using Majorana representations. The analysis focuses on its behavior near the disorder line defined by $\gamma^2 + h^2 = 1$.
key_observables: Bulk penetration of $n$-particle modes, non-zero and constant correlation functions on the DL, and the superconductivity order parameter ($\mathcal{O}_{	ext{sc}}^2$).
important_parameters: The disorder line (DL) defined by $\gamma^2 + h^2 = 1$, and the number of penetrating Majorana particles ($n \ge 2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to zero temperature ($T=0$) and focuses on specific factorized ground states $|\Psi_\pmangle$ constructed on the DL.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the phase diagram, explicitly marking the disorder line (DL) as the circle $h^2 + \gamma^2 = 1$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the Hamiltonian and transforming it to Majorana fermions. It then analyzes correlation functions ($\langle i b_{m} a_{n} angle$) in different regimes, culminating in specific results for the DL where bulk penetration is observed.
why_interesting: The study of topological phases like those exhibiting Majorana modes is central to condensed matter theory and quantum computation; understanding how correlations behave at critical points (like the DL) provides insight into robust physical properties.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The phase diagram of the model on the (γ, h) plane at T = 0. It has three gapped phases: polarized (P) |h| > 1; ferromagnetic (FM) |h| < 1; mx ̸= 0 (γ > 0) and my ̸= 0 (γ < 0). The model is critical (gapless) on the phase boundaries: (i) two infinite lines h = ±1 (dark blue); (ii) segment |h| ≤1 at γ = 0 (magenta). The disorder line is the circle h2 + γ2 = 1 (dashed red).
